hairs-on-head.why: Source gives 110,000 for brown hair; a hair is a part everyone pictures the same, and colour changing the count is a real reveal. Fact: 'red heads' -> 'redheads'.

breath-hold-record.why: AIDA 11:35 (2009) is the official record, and the oxygen record makes a good reveal; definition jargon 'AIDA static apnea' -> 'official freediving record'.

eyeball-width.why: Source: width 24.2 mm, typical adult 24 mm; something everyone can picture, and the fact (16-17 mm at birth) teaches.

liver-weight.why: Source states about 1.5 kg; easy -> false (few people have an anchor for organ weights); fact now says 'heaviest internal organ', as the source does, without the odd 'though'.

ostrich-egg-weight.why: Source: average 1.4 kg; easy to picture, and 'smallest egg relative to the mother' is a good twist.

arctic-tern-migration.why: 70,900 km average for Greenland/Iceland birds, pinned by the definition; reasonable from pole-to-pole and back, and bigger than you'd think.

emperor-penguin-dive.why: Lead says 535 m, body says 564 m deepest (1994): 1.05x apart, and 'deepest dive recorded' pins 564; a surprising depth.

hummingbird-heart-rate.why: Source: 1,260 bpm in a blue-throated hummingbird; reasoned from a human's 70, and the torpor contrast is in the source.

cheetah-top-speed.why: 104 km/h is the source's highest reliable figure (lead range 93-104), and the definition says so; acceleration fact checks out.

burj-khalifa-height.why: Duplicate: the live bank already has burj-khalifa-height (829.8 m to the tip).

great-pyramid-height.why: Source: 146.6 m as built (138.5 m today), definition says which; 3,700 years as the tallest is a great reveal.

pisa-tower-height.why: Source: 55.86 m low side, 56.67 m high side, definition pins it; the 3.9 m lean is a good reveal.

hong-kong-zhuhai-macau-bridge.why: Source: 55 km whole crossing (main bridge 29.6 km), definition pins it; 'longest sea crossing' rewards a guess.

mid-levels-escalator-climb.why: Obscure outside Hong Kong: the vertical climb of an 18-escalator system is unclear to anyone who hasn't seen it, and the source only says 'over 135 m'.

bering-strait-width.why: Source: about 82 km mainland to mainland, definition rules out the Diomede islands, which the fact then reveals (3.8 km).

greenland-population.why: Source: 56,542 in 2025, dated; a huge island with a small town's population is a good surprise.

trans-siberian-length.why: Source: 9,289 km Moscow-Vladivostok; reasoned from Russia's width, and the eight time zones fact is in the source.

antarctica-winter-population.why: Source: about 1,000 in winter, 4,000 in summer; definition says who is counted; few people on a whole continent surprises.

sun-width-in-earths.why: Source: diameter about 109 times Earth's, definition says diameters; a fair ratio to reason about.

olympus-mons-height.why: Figures run 21.3 to 26 km (1.2x); 'above the Martian surface' matches the source's 'nearly 22 km'; Italy-sized base fact is true.

saturn-v-height.why: Source: 111 m with the Apollo spacecraft, definition pins it; first-stage fact checks out.

mars-year.why: Source: 687 Earth days, definition says Earth days; a fair classic, seasons fact in the source.

giant-pumpkin-record.why: Source table: 1,431.5 kg (Oct 2026); the record moves yearly but the definition dates it; 23 kg a day fact checks out.

jackfruit-weight.why: Source says up to 50 kg twice; the question asks the maximum and the definition says so; largest tree fruit is a good reveal.

hot-dog-eating-record.why: Source: 76 HDB in 10 min (2021), the contest record, definition pins it; Kobayashi doubling 25.5 is a great fact.

baguette-length.why: Source: usual length about 65 cm; a good opener everyone has held, and the 1.8 m loaves fact teaches.

gold-bar-weight.why: Source: 400 oz Good Delivery bar is 12.4 kg; heavier than the movie bar people picture, definition pins which bar.

longest-flight-distance.why: Source table: SQ 23 JFK-Singapore 15,349 km; dated 2026 so it stays true when Project Sunrise starts; route lets a player reason.

ever-given-length.why: Source: 399.94 m length overall; everyone pictures the ship in the canal, fact on the six-day blockage checks out.

everest-height.why: Source: 8,848.86 m (2020 survey), dated; classic opener, and the snow-cap argument is in the source.

tallest-tree-height.why: Source: Hyperion 116.22 m in 2026, dated; 67 cm of growth since 2006 matches 115.55 m then.

lake-baikal-depth.why: Source: 1,642 m maximum depth; more water than the Great Lakes combined is in the source and explains the depth.

bamboo-growth.why: Source gives 91 cm (Guinness) and also 120 cm observed, so 'fastest reported' pointed at the wrong figure; definition now 'Guinness record, in 24 hours'.

great-barrier-reef-length.why: Source: over 2,300 km; reasoned from Australia's coast, 2,900 reefs and 900 islands teaches.

mercury-litre-weight.why: Density 13.546 g/cm3 near room temperature is exactly 13.546 kg a litre (answer was rounded to 13.5); fact now ties the lighthouse lenses to the density.

earth-spin-speed.why: Source states 1,674.7 km/h (answer was cut to 1674); a player can work it out from 40,000 km in a day, and the 45 degree fact is in the source.

inner-core-temperature.why: Source: about 5,430 C, estimates 5,100-5,960 (1.2x); 'as hot as the Sun's surface' is the source's own comparison.

candle-flame-temperature.why: Source: about 1,400 C in the hottest zone; hotter than people think, and the yellow-is-cooler fact is in the source.

bolt-top-speed.why: Source: 44.72 km/h from his 60-80 m split in the 9.58 run, average 37.58; a good opener to reason about.

high-jump-record.why: Source: 2.45 m, Sotomayor 1993, never beaten; easy to picture against a person.

badminton-smash-speed.why: Source: 426 km/h in a match vs the 263 km/h tennis serve; 'in a match' excludes lab records.

world-cup-trophy-weight.why: Source: 6.175 kg; the hollow vs 70-80 kg solid-gold fact is a great reveal.

table-tennis-ball-weight.why: Source: rules say 2.7 g; an object everyone has held, fair opener, bounce rule is in the source.

terracotta-army-size.why: Source: more than 8,000 soldiers (2007 estimate), definition dates it; a soldier is a part anyone pictures the same.

david-statue-height.why: Source: 5.17 m, measured exactly only in 1998-99; much bigger than people picture.

bayeux-tapestry-length.why: Source: 68.38 m long, about 50 cm tall; a strip far longer than the word 'tapestry' suggests, and the fact explains why.

hollywood-sign-letters.why: Source lead: 45 ft (13.7 m), body 44 ft (13.4 m), 1.02x apart; HOLLYWOODLAND fact checks out.

woodstock-crowd.why: Source: 460,000 to 500,000 (1.09x); 'high estimate' says which end, and half a million is how it's remembered; 50,000 expected is in the source.

nile-length.why: Source: about 6,650 km, same as TENtacle's rivers list; the Amazon dispute fact is in the source.

shanghai-metro-trips.why: Source: 3,773.8 million rides (2024), exactly 3.7738 billion (answer was rounded to 3.77); top of TENtacle's metro list.
